record.context_brief: Prompt dimuon baseline in proton-nucleus collisions
record.original_question: Can proton-nucleus measurements determine the non-thermal prompt dimuon baseline in the intermediate mass region well enough to distinguish genuine thermal dimuon production in heavy-ion collisions, given that low-mass Drell-Yan production is not reliably calculable and may be enhanced in proton-nucleus and nucleus-nucleus collisions by interactions involving extra partons from the colliding hadrons?

evidence.quote: the Drell-Yan yields are not theoretically calculable in a reliable way for such low values of the dimuon mass, where higher order effects may be more important than at higher masses.

Without having this possible source of prompt dimuons under control, through a detailed analysis of proton-nucleus data, there is little hope that we can find clear evidence for thermal dimuon production in heavy-ion data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider high-energy hadronic collisions producing prompt muon pairs (dimuons) in the intermediate invariant-mass region 1 GeV/c² < M_{μμ} < 2.5 GeV/c². In this region the observed prompt dimuon yield in heavy-ion (nucleus–nucleus) collisions is expected to contain:

(i) a Drell–Yan contribution (q q̄ → γ* → μ⁺μ⁻, including possible higher-order partonic corrections and contributions involving additional partons from the colliding hadrons),
(ii) correlated semileptonic decays of D D̄ pairs (open charm),
(iii) a putative "thermal" component originating from a hot, possibly partonic, medium produced in the collision.

The Drell–Yan cross section at such low dimuon masses is not reliably calculable from perturbative QCD because higher-order effects are large, and nuclear effects (e.g., extra-parton interactions in pA and AA) may enhance it relative to a pp extrapolation.

Problem. Determine whether measurements of prompt dimuon production in proton–nucleus (pA) collisions, used as a non-thermal baseline, can be made precise and theoretically controlled enough to fix the non-thermal prompt dimuon yield (Drell–Yan plus correlated open-charm decays, including possible nuclear-enhancement effects) in the intermediate-mass region 1 GeV/c² < M_{μμ} < 2.5 GeV/c² with sufficient accuracy that an excess in nucleus–nucleus collisions over this pA-based baseline constitutes unambiguous evidence for genuine thermal dimuon production.

Equivalently: Is it possible, using only pA data together with current or foreseeable theoretical inputs, to subtract the non-thermal prompt dimuon contribution in AA collisions in the intermediate-mass region to a precision that isolates a thermal signal?
artifact.category_tag: Thermal dimuon production in heavy-ion collisions
artifact.status_search_result: NA60 measurements in In–In collisions at 158 A GeV established that, after subtracting the Drell–Yan and open-charm contributions calibrated on proton–nucleus data, a prompt excess remains in the intermediate-mass region 1 < M < 2.5 GeV/c², interpreted as evidence for thermal dimuons of partonic origin. This addresses the question affirmatively at SPS energies in the regime studied, but a fully theoretically controlled pA baseline (including possible extra-parton enhancements of low-mass Drell–Yan) remains an active topic, with the proposed NA60+ experiment aiming to improve precision. Hence the question is partially resolved rather than fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Evidence for the production of thermal muon pairs with masses above 1 GeV/c² in 158 A GeV indium-indium collisions
status_evidence.snippet: The yield of muon pairs in the mass region 1<M<2.5 GeV/c² produced in In–In collisions significantly exceeds the sum of Drell–Yan dimuons and muon pairs from D-meson decays. These sources properly account for the dimuons produced in proton–nucleus collisions.
status_evidence.claim: pA data fix the non-thermal baseline, and an excess remains in AA, supporting a thermal interpretation.

status_evidence.title: NA60+ physics performance studies
status_evidence.snippet: The invariant-mass spectrum is described as a sum of light-hadron decays, Drell–Yan, semileptonic decays of charm hadron pairs, and thermal dimuons; improved precision is targeted in the intermediate-mass region.
status_evidence.claim: Further pA-based baseline determination and thermal-dimuon characterization remain active goals.

status_evidence.title: Low mass dimuon production in proton-nucleus collisions with the NA60 apparatus
status_evidence.snippet: NA60 measurement of dimuon production in p–A collisions providing baseline for heavy-ion comparisons.
status_evidence.claim: pA dimuon baselines have been measured experimentally.
